answer: Escrowed reputation cooling curve. Each new identity funds an escrow that unlocks against sustained activity: full balance returns only after N verified transactions spanning a minimum time span, and early withdrawal forfeits a growing fraction. Attackers must harbor capital locked for the whole span per fake identity, so mass fabrication becomes a slow capital sink. A marble of reputation accrues per completed cycle, and where a sybil farm floods one canyon of the graph, its marginal escrow cost scales with local identity density, taxing the attacker where concentration pays.
